closure_explanation: Theorem 5.1 (thm:optimal_ringmaster_dynamic) is proved (Appendix E, lines 1391-1440) from Theorem 4.1 (thm:ringmaster_iteration, a standalone convergence result, hence public), Lemma 5.1 (lem:time_R_dyn) applied Kbar times, and the WLOG footnote justified by Appendix F (sec:l_init, node SF). Theorem 4.1 is proved from Lemma C.1 (lemma:descent) and Lemma C.2 (lemma:residual). Lemma 5.1's proof reuses the argument of the proof of Lemma 4.1 (lem:time_R) up to (RQKxmnzvrIUDaroZE); that argument is part of L51's own proof and Lemma 4.1's statement (fixed computation model) is not used, so Lemma 4.1 is excluded. Statements use Algorithm 5 (alg:ringmasternewstops, as requested by the user), Assumptions 1-3 (A1-A3), the universal computation model (MODU), 'any computation model' for Theorem 4.1 (MODA), the definitions of T(R,T_0)/T_K (TDEF) and the problem/eps-stationarity definitions (PROB). Derived supporting nodes: DSTOCH (measure-theoretic steps of the proofs of C.1/C.2), DREC (the analytic core of Theorem 4.1 for the delayed recursion), DEXEC (template execution of Algorithm 5 = delayed recursion with delays <= R-1), DDEAD (the iteration of Lemma 5.1 in the proof of Theorem 5.1). Excluded: Algorithms 1-4 (Asynchronous SGD, Rennala SGD, Naive Optimal ASGD, Ringmaster without stops; the user requested Algorithm 5; Algorithm 1 only supplies the delay notation recorded in ALG5), Theorem 2.1 (naive method), Lemma 4.1 and Theorem 4.2 (fixed computation model), the adaptive stepsize reformulation (eq:adapative_step_size, describes Algorithm 4), Appendix D (example derivations), experiments, and citations to lower bounds (tyurin2024tighttimecomplexitiesparallel, optimality remarks are not part of the formal claim). Convergence results in the closure: T41 and T51. Updated interface adaptation: fresh review under protocol version 3; keep the exact source dependency closure and original analytic results. Derive natural horizons from supplied gap upper bounds, return a single random point for iteration accuracy and a point/clock pair for time accuracy, expose integrals inline, and move only the existing finite-deadline premise to the public time domain. Reuse proved library dependencies after fresh correspondence checks; old approvals are not reused.

classification.reason: Problem formulation of the introduction: the stochastic optimization problem, the n workers and the notion of an eps-stationary point; no claim.

clauses.text: The problem is min_{x in R^d} f(x); worker i in [n] can compute stochastic gradients grad f(x; xi) with xi ~ D.

clauses.justification: Introduction: the goal of nonconvex optimization.
clauses.text: A random vector xbar in R^d is an eps-stationary point if E[||grad f(xbar)||^2] <= eps.

interpretations.decision: Only the oracle grad f(x; xi) and the law D enter the analysis; the representation f(x) = E f(x; xi) is not used beyond Assumption 3.

nodes.statement: Minimize f(x) = E_{xi ~ D}[f(x; xi)] over x in R^d. Stochastic gradients grad f(x; xi) with xi ~ D are available to n workers, each with access to the same distribution D. An eps-stationary point is a (random) vector xbar in R^d with E[||grad f(xbar)||^2] <= eps; ||.|| is the Euclidean norm.

interpretations.effect_on_scope: The joint law of the applied stochastic gradients is the one of the source; measurability and integrability of the oracle are the standard conditions making the expectations defined.

For a measurable function Phi of (xi_0, ..., xi_{k-1}) and xi_k, E[Phi] = E[int Phi(xi_0..xi_{k-1}, b) dD(b)] whenever Phi(., xi_k) is integrable (tower property with the fresh independent sample xi_k).

clauses.justification: Variance decomposition in the proof of C.1; finiteness of the expectations used throughout.

E||sum_{j=b}^{m-1} (grad f(x^{a_j}; xi_j) - grad f(x^{a_j}))||^2 <= (m - b) sigma^2.
